facts.raw_span: A 47-year-old Caucasian woman
23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis
four episodes of optic neuritis since 1989
longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis in 1995
persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) oligoclonal bands
unremarkable brain MRI scans
subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis
expressive language impairment and 3/5 strength in the right arm and leg
normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter
serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre was 1:1000 by cell-based assay
no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis, no oligoclonal bands, and a normal cell count
A 47-year-old Caucasian woman
23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis
four episodes of optic neuritis since 1989
longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis in 1995
persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) oligoclonal bands
unremarkable brain MRI scans
subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis
expressive language impairment and 3/5 strength in the right arm and leg
normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter
serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre was 1:1000 by cell-based assay
no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis, no oligoclonal bands, and a normal cell count

concepts.why: The patient's history of optic neuritis and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, combined with the presence of a large T2-hyperintense lesion and a high serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre, supports this diagnosis.

The patient's 23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis, characterized by episodes of optic neuritis and transverse myelitis, initially suggests this diagnosis, although the lack of oligoclonal bands and the presence of aquaporin-4 antibodies complicate this picture.

The large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter could be consistent with a tumefactive variant of multiple sclerosis, although the clinical and laboratory findings also suggest other possibilities.

The subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis, combined with the presence of a large T2-hyperintense lesion, could suggest acute disseminated encephalomyelitis, although the patient's history and laboratory findings are not entirely typical for this condition.
It explains the uncovered finding of persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands and no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis.

rationales.F04: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis is a characteristic feature of Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
rationales.F05: The absence of oligoclonal bands in the cerebrospinal fluid is more typical of Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder than Multiple sclerosis.
rationales.F11: The presence of aquaporin-4 antibodies is a specific marker for Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a high serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre and a history of longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, along with optic neuritis episodes, strongly supports Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, despite the patient's initial presumed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis.
